text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgarian citizens' deposits in commercial banks will not be blocked in case of future bank bankruptcies, a socialist party deputy said in parliament.
He added that options for issuing high-yield treasury securities to guarantee citizens' deposits in banks under special supervision had been discussed.
-- Bulgaria's state-owned tobacco holding Bulgartabak will offer for mass privatisation a 20 percent stake in seven tobacco companies, holding chairman Spas Gelemerov said.
-- A group working on Bulgaria's joining the World Trade Organisation (WTO) has approved the country's credentials for membership, 24 Chasa's Geneva correspondent said.
In order to receive full membership Bulgaria's candidature should be approved by the WTO's General Council, he said.
-- Valentina Manolova and Valentin Minev are Capitalbank's new executive directors, the bank's board chairman Angel Parvanov said.

-- Bulgaria is running out of pork due to large exports, the association of meat-processors' chairman Roumen Kuzmanov said. Over 5,000 tonnes of pork were exported to Macedonia, Russia and the former Soviet republics last month, experts said.
-- Sofia airport's runway repairs will cost some 120 million levs, twice the initial estimate, due to price hikes in fuel, electricity and construction materials, its director said.
-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency (PA) said it expected offers within two weeks for the sale of 60 percent of the Devnya-based chemical giant Sodi.

-- The Industrial Bank of Japan's representatives arrive in Bulgaria today for talks with the cabinet on Bulgaria's refusal to cover maturity payments on Samurai bonds worth $50 million issued in 1989 by Mineralbank, which is now under special supervision.
-- Bulgaria's debt-ridden National Electricity Company (NEC) plans to borrow four million dollars from the Dutch ING Bank to pay for spare parts and repairs, NEC officials said.
-- Bulgaria's Foreign Minister Georgi Pirinski has demanded at a closed-door cabinet meeting on Sunday that the people responsible for the deep economic crisis should be identified.
-- Bulgaria's electricity prices for households are expected to rise by 17 percent in October, deputies said.
